100m: Male Elite champion: Caleb Riley (🇺🇸 United States) in 38.202.
Female Elite champion: Elizabeth Polsgrove (🇺🇸 United States) in 30.982.
Fastest recorded 100m run: Luke Beckstrand in 24.542 during the Semi Final.
Knockout podiums follow bracket progression: semifinal winners contest gold and silver, while semifinal losers contest bronze.
The Final column contains both the championship final and the third-place race; their times are not pooled into one ranking.
Adaptive categories and Female Veteran without semifinals are treated as direct finals using the supplied Best Time.
100m-team: Fastest team in the supplied data: Usa 100m Elite Mixed Team (🇺🇸 United States) in 27.874.
Medal-table leader: 🇺🇸 United States with 6 gold and 10 total medals.
400m-team: Fastest team in the supplied data: USA 400m Mixed U16 Team F (🇺🇸 United States) in 1:34.370.
Medal-table leader: 🇺🇸 United States with 5 gold and 12 total medals.
The fastest 400m team time came from a U16 team, quicker than every Elite team in the supplied team dataset.
xc-team: Fastest team in the supplied data: NED XC Elite Male Team (🇳🇱 Netherlands) in 32:40.9.
Medal-table leader: 🇺🇸 United States with 4 gold and 12 total medals.
400m: Male Elite champion: Daniel Ekström (🇸🇪 Sweden) in 1:49.351.
Female Elite champion: Patrycja Teska (🇵🇱 Poland) in 2:22.175.
Fastest recorded 400m run: Cameron Godbout in 1:37.468 during the Final.
Elite athletes progressed through a Round of 12 and Round of 6; other divisions used the supplied rounds as applicable.
Categories marked “No Final” use the time supplied in parentheses in the finals workbook as a direct-final result.
short: Fastest ranked man: Goncalo Prudencio (🇵🇹 Portugal) in 14:31.0.
Fastest ranked woman: Elsa Rijpstra (🇳🇱 Netherlands) in 17:38.2.
15.3% of timed finishers were DNC (113 athletes).
Only 11.9 seconds separated the Male Elite gold and bronze.
standard: Fastest ranked man: Stijn Lagrand (🇳🇱 Netherlands) in 40:39.6.
Fastest ranked woman: Elsa Rijpstra (🇳🇱 Netherlands) in 46:19.5.
29.0% of timed finishers were DNC (151 athletes).
Female Standard DNC rate was 45.8% versus 21.0% for men.
Elsa Rijpstra won Female Elite in both Short and Standard Course.

overallFacts: 1077 unique athletes are linked across the supplied individual and team datasets.
834 athletes appear in two or more event types.
Jamie Gane, Lena Schollig and Stephan Wirtz appear in all seven event types in the available data.
🇺🇸 United States leads the combined medal table with 44 golds and 118 total medals.
Among delegations with at least 10 linked athletes, 🇵🇹 Portugal has the highest medals-per-athlete ratio (0.85).

dataNotes.title: 400m elimination and final method
dataNotes.text: 400m stages are linked to the qualification field by normalized athlete name and exact division. Podiums use the supplied finals times; where the export says “No Final”, the parenthetical time is treated as the direct-final result.

dataNotes.title: DNC definition
dataNotes.text: For Short and Standard Course, DNC means the athlete finished the course but failed 3 or more obstacles. They retain a finish time but are unranked and ineligible for medals.

dataNotes.title: Team medal method
dataNotes.text: 100m Team Relay and 400m Team Relay podiums are calculated from the Best Time column across the supplied Q1/Q2 team attempts. Open categories are excluded.

dataNotes.title: 100m knockout and direct-final method
dataNotes.text: For bracket divisions, semifinal winners contest gold and silver while semifinal losers contest bronze. The Final column therefore contains two separate head-to-head races and is not ranked as one pooled list. Divisions without semifinals use the supplied Best Time as a direct final.

dataNotes.title: Country normalization
dataNotes.text: Native country labels in the timing exports (for example Sverige, Polska and Nederland/Holland) are normalized to standard English names while the original results remain traceable to their source files.
